qdc3aa50e.question: Integration gap (non-blocking, HLD-aligned): this LLD exposes writeCheckpoint/readCheckpoint/finalizeAndCleanup and proves them in isolation, but wiring them into s1's own round-driver cycle (calling writeCheckpoint after each completed unit, readCheckpoint before starting a resumed review, and finalizeAndCleanup at a terminal state) is s1's own adjacent-boundary responsibility, not built here.

summary.prose: This Story adds the review checkpoint record (sc5): a small, independent JSON side-record under each review's own .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder, written automatically once per completed round or Task so a crash costs at most one unit of rework, plus a final step that copies a completed review's last output into durable storage before its scratch folder is deleted. The round-driver (s1, owned elsewhere) calls these functions; this Story only exposes and proves them.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Alternative a2 wins: one shared round-driver function in a new sibling module under src/workflow/ (outside review-history/, which is being retired from rather than extended) takes a small per-review-type hook set -- the grounding/findings call, checkpoint granularity, and finding taxonomy/severity -- and runs the identical round cycle, checkpoint lifecycle, and reconciliation call for every review type.

ownedContracts.name: Review checkpoint record
ownedContracts.purpose: The generic 'review checkpoint' JSON side-record and the .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder lifecycle (per-review-type granularity, durable copy before deletion, reviewId as one identity), per k1/k7/k8/lc4.

consumedContracts.name: Review-type hook set
consumedContracts.purpose: The small hook set (grounding/findings call, checkpoint granularity, taxonomy/severity) that is the only thing legitimately differing per review type, consumed by the round-driver, per the Epic's one-shared-process framing (Story s1 ac1/ac2).

boundary.internal: The exact per-review-type granularity mapping (round-level for design review, per-Task for code review) and the durable-copy-before-deletion mechanics stay internal to s5; no other Story's type depends on ReviewCheckpoint's internals beyond what sc1's round-driver needs to call it.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The round-driver function itself -- what it does internally to run the grounding+findings, reconciliation, render+present and checkpoint-write cycle -- stays private to s1; no other Story's type depends on the driver's internals, only on the hook contract sc1 exposes.

Which exact per-review-type severity scales exist beyond the HIGH/MED default, and how a review type's Feedback implementation declares its own, stay internal to s2; no other Story's type depends on Finding's shape.

How the reconciliation LLM call is actually prompted, and how it reads the temp folder's audit trail when needed, stay internal to s3; no other Story's type depends on ReconciliationResult's internals beyond its verdict shape.

The exact docgen docType registration and MD rendering logic (including the resolved/still-open/contradicted annotation rule scoped to this round's own corrections) stay internal to s4; no other Story's type depends on the renderer's internals.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase B — taxonomy, reconciliation, rendering, checkpointing

nonFunctional.performance: Checkpoint write/read (sc5) is a single small JSON file write/read per completed unit of work (a round, or a Task), adding no I/O beyond what the round cycle already performs.
nonFunctional.durability: The final round's review-output JSON is copied into durable artifact storage before the .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder is deleted at a terminal state (k7), so a completed review's result survives after the ephemeral working folder is gone.

summary.prose: This Story adds the review checkpoint record (sc5): a small, independent JSON side-record under each review's own .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder, written automatically once per completed round or Task so a crash costs at most one unit of rework, plus a final step that copies a completed review's last output into durable storage before its scratch folder is deleted. The round-driver (s1, owned elsewhere) calls these functions; this Story only exposes and proves them.

api.name: writeCheckpoint
api.signature: function writeCheckpoint(reviewId: string, lastCompletedUnit: { readonly kind: 'round' | 'task'; readonly ref: number | string }): Promise<void>

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.purpose: The review's own identity -- the same literal string already used to name its .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder in reconciliation.ts and review-report.ts.

parameters.name: lastCompletedUnit
parameters.type: { readonly kind: 'round' | 'task'; readonly ref: number | string }
parameters.purpose: The unit of work (a round number, or a Task's own reference) that just finished -- supplied by the caller (s1's driver), never derived here, per ac1's per-review-type granularity rule.

returns.meaning: Resolves once the checkpoint.json file has been durably written; rejects if the write fails.

errors.condition: reviewId is not a literal identifier (fails the same path-traversal check reconciliation.ts and review-report.ts already apply).
the reviewed repository cannot be resolved (no registered repo for the request's cwd, and no INSRC_REPO fallback).

preconditions: reviewId names an existing (or about-to-exist) .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ review directory.
postconditions: A ReviewCheckpoint JSON record exists at .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/checkpoint.json containing exactly {reviewId, lastCompletedUnit}, overwriting any prior checkpoint for the same reviewId.

api.name: readCheckpoint
api.signature: function readCheckpoint(reviewId: string): Promise<{ readonly reviewId: string; readonly lastCompletedUnit: { readonly kind: 'round' | 'task'; readonly ref: number | string } } | undefined>

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.purpose: The review's own identity to look up a prior checkpoint for.

returns.meaning: The last-written ReviewCheckpoint for this reviewId, or undefined when no checkpoint file exists yet (a review that has never completed a unit of work).

errors.condition: reviewId is not a literal identifier.
the reviewed repository cannot be resolved.

postconditions: Never throws merely because no checkpoint exists yet -- that is the defined undefined case (ac2: a fresh review resumes from the start, not an error).

api.name: finalizeAndCleanup
api.signature: function finalizeAndCleanup(reviewId: string, finalOutput: unknown): Promise<void>

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.purpose: The review's own identity, naming both the .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder to delete and the durable artifact location to copy into.

parameters.name: finalOutput
parameters.purpose: The final round's own review-output JSON (the caller's self-contained finding/reconciliation result for its last round) to persist durably before the scratch folder is gone.

returns.meaning: Resolves once the durable copy has been written AND the .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder has been deleted, in that order.

errors.condition: reviewId is not a literal identifier.
the reviewed repository cannot be resolved.
the durable copy write fails -- the temp folder is NOT deleted in this case, preserving k7's ordering invariant.

preconditions: The review has reached a terminal state (the caller decides this; this function does not itself judge terminality).
postconditions: finalOutput is durably persisted before .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ is deleted, never the reverse order, matching k7 exactly.
A deletion failure (e.g. a concurrent process holding a file open) still leaves the durable copy intact, since the copy already completed first.

errorCases.detection: A literal-identifier regex check (the same pattern reconciliation.ts's requireValidReviewId and review-report.ts's requireValidReviewId already apply) run first, before any path join or filesystem access.
errorCases.response: Throws a plain Error naming the invalid reviewId, before any directory is touched.
errorCases.userImpact: The call fails fast with a clear message instead of silently joining an unsafe path.

errorCases.scenario: The reviewed repository cannot be resolved (no registered repo for the request's cwd, and no INSRC_REPO fallback)
errorCases.detection: resolveRepoPath(undefined) returns undefined, exactly as reconciliation.ts's and review-report.ts's own defaultResolveRepoRoot already detect.
errorCases.response: Throws a plain Error naming the resolution failure, before any filesystem access.
errorCases.userImpact: The call fails fast rather than silently defaulting to the daemon process's own cwd.

errorCases.scenario: An existing path segment between the repo root and the checkpoint file (the reviewId directory, .insrc/tmp itself, or the checkpoint.json leaf) is a symlink -- whether planted maliciously or substituted by a race after an earlier check
errorCases.detection: A requireNoSymlinkInPath-style walk (reusing review-report.ts's own lstatSync-based, dangling-symlink-safe helper verbatim) runs immediately before every write.
errorCases.response: Throws an Error naming the symlinked segment; refuses to write through it.
errorCases.userImpact: A checkpoint write can never be redirected outside the repository or truncate an unrelated file via a symlinked review directory or checkpoint file.

errorCases.scenario: writeCheckpoint's own write is interrupted mid-write (process killed, disk full) between opening the file and completing the write
errorCases.detection: Not detected at write time -- prevented structurally: writeCheckpoint publishes through the same guarded temp-file-then-rename primitive review-report.ts's P2 fix established (publishGuarded), so an observer can only ever see the complete prior checkpoint or the complete new one, never a partially-written file.
errorCases.response: No special handling needed at the write site; the rename is atomic.
errorCases.userImpact: A crash during a checkpoint write can never leave behind a checkpoint that reads back as corrupted, preserving ac2's 'at most one unit of rework' guarantee.

errorCases.scenario: readCheckpoint finds a checkpoint.json file that is not valid JSON, or is valid JSON but does not match ReviewCheckpoint's shape (e.g. truncated by something outside this Story's own write path, or disk-level corruption)
errorCases.detection: JSON.parse throws, or the parsed value fails a minimal shape check (reviewId is a string, lastCompletedUnit.kind is 'round' or 'task').
errorCases.response: Treated identically to a missing checkpoint: readCheckpoint resolves to undefined rather than throwing or returning unvalidated data, so a review can always still resume (from the start, in the worst case) rather than being permanently stuck on an unreadable checkpoint.
errorCases.userImpact: A corrupted checkpoint costs at most a full restart of the review, never a hard failure that blocks resumption entirely -- consistent with ac2's crash-safety intent even in this worse-than-expected case.

errorCases.scenario: finalizeAndCleanup's durable copy write fails (disk full, permission denied, symlink refusal) partway through
errorCases.detection: The write call itself throws or rejects.
errorCases.response: Propagates the error unchanged; the .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ deletion step is never reached.
errorCases.userImpact: A review whose final output could not be durably copied keeps its scratch folder intact rather than losing the only copy of its result -- k7's ordering is preserved even on failure.

errorCases.scenario: finalizeAndCleanup's deletion step encounters a symlinked .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ directory (the exact leaf path itself redirected elsewhere)
errorCases.detection: The same requireNoSymlinkInPath-style walk (lstat-based, never following) runs immediately before the recursive delete, exactly as before the write.
errorCases.response: Throws an Error naming the symlink; refuses to delete through it (never follows a symlinked directory into a deletion that could remove unrelated real files elsewhere).
errorCases.userImpact: A symlinked scratch folder can never cause finalizeAndCleanup to delete something outside the review's own .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ location.

edgeCases.input: readCheckpoint called for a reviewId that has never had writeCheckpoint called (a brand-new review, or one whose .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ directory does not exist at all)
edgeCases.expected: Resolves to undefined, not an error -- the caller (s1's driver) starts from round 1 / the first Task.

edgeCases.input: finalizeAndCleanup called a second time for a reviewId whose .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder was already deleted by an earlier successful call (e.g. a retried completion after a crash between the durable copy and the deletion)
edgeCases.expected: The durable copy write re-runs (idempotent overwrite of the same durable location with the same finalOutput) and the deletion step is a no-op when the folder no longer exists, rather than throwing -- mirrors the force:true convention this codebase's own tests already use for .insrc/tmp cleanup.

edgeCases.input: finalizeAndCleanup called when checkpoint.json was never written at all (e.g. a single-round design review that completed its only round without ever crashing, so no intermediate checkpoint was needed)
edgeCases.expected: Succeeds regardless -- finalizeAndCleanup deletes whatever the .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder currently contains (checkpoint.json, round outputs, rendered reports) as a whole; it does not require a checkpoint to have existed.

edgeCases.input: writeCheckpoint called repeatedly for the same reviewId as successive rounds/Tasks complete
edgeCases.expected: Each call overwrites the prior checkpoint.json with the new lastCompletedUnit -- only the single most recent checkpoint is ever kept, never a growing history.

invariantsToPreserve.text: Checkpoint granularity is defined per review type (round-level for design review, per-Task for code review), never re-derived inside this Story's own functions -- the caller always supplies lastCompletedUnit.kind.
Checkpoint write/read is automatic and internal to the review process, never an agent-driven step.
The .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ temp folder is deleted only after the final round's review-output JSON is copied into durable artifact storage, never before.

reviewId is one identity: the same string names both the .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder and the reviewId field inside the checkpoint record itself, so a resume can recover the id from the checkpoint artifact's own content.

alternativesConsidered.name: Standalone checkpoint module: three exported functions over a flat JSON side-record
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: writeCheckpoint / readCheckpoint / finalizeAndCleanup in a new checkpoint.ts, exactly matching sc5's interfaceSketch and lc4's 'independent JSON side-record' requirement.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add src/workflow/review-round/checkpoint.ts exporting: `writeCheckpoint(reviewId, lastCompletedUnit)` -- writes `.insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/checkpoint.json` containing exactly `ReviewCheckpoint` (`{reviewId, lastCompletedUnit: {kind, ref}}`), overwriting any prior checkpoint for the same reviewId (ac1, no agent-driven step -- s1's driver calls this once per completed round/Task). `readCheckpoint(reviewId)` -- reads it back, returning `undefined` when no checkpoint file exists yet (a fresh review), so a caller (s1's driver, on resume) knows whether to start from round 1 or from `lastCompletedUnit`'s own next unit (ac2, ac4). `finalizeAndCleanup(reviewId, finalOutput)` -- copies the final round's review-output JSON into the review's durable artifact storage location, THEN deletes the `.insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/` folder (ac3), reusing review-report.ts's and reconciliation.ts's own established symlink-safety pattern (lstat-based containment checks before any write or recursive delete, since an attacker-substituted symlink at any of these three operations -- checkpoint write, durable copy, or folder deletion -- could redirect outside the repo or delete/overwrite an unrelated path). reviewId is the sole identity (ac4): every function takes it as a bare string, exactly as runReviewRound already does, with no ReviewContext struct involved (per s1's own analyzeBundles finding -- no such type exists).
pros: Smallest module that fully satisfies all four acceptance criteria and lc4's explicit side-record independence requirement

Mirrors the established conventions in reconciliation.ts and review-report.ts verbatim (repo resolution, symlink-safety, injectable test-deps seam), so reviewers and future maintainers read one consistent idiom across the whole review-round/ module

Checkpoint granularity (round vs task) is read from the caller-supplied lastCompletedUnit.kind, not re-derived here -- this module stays a dumb, generic side-record, exactly as sc5's own boundary.internal note requires ('no other Story's type depends on ReviewCheckpoint's internals')
cons: s1's driver (private internals, adjacent boundary) must be the one to actually call writeCheckpoint/readCheckpoint/finalizeAndCleanup at the right points in its own cycle -- this Story can only expose the functions and prove them correct in isolation, not wire them into driver.ts itself, so an integration gap could remain until s1's own driver is updated (flagged as an openQuestion / HLD-aligned note, not built around here)

Three separate small functions rather than one object -- slightly more surface area than a single class, though each function is independently testable and each acceptance criterion maps to exactly one of them

alternativesConsidered.name: Fold checkpoint read/write into the round-driver's own call signature
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Instead of standalone functions, give runReviewRound itself new checkpoint-aware parameters/return fields, so the driver reads/writes checkpoints inline.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Extend runReviewRound's own signature (or an internal helper inside driver.ts) to read a prior checkpoint before the round loop starts and write one after each unit completes, folding sc5's logic directly into s1's driver rather than exposing it as a separate consumable module.
pros: No separate call site needed in the driver -- checkpointing happens 'for free' as part of calling runReviewRound
Avoids the a1 integration-gap con, since the write/read calls are already inside the one function that needs them
cons: Violates the HLD's own adjacent-boundary rule: 'the round-driver function itself... stays private to s1; no other Story's type depends on the driver's internals' -- this alternative requires s5 to edit s1's owned driver.ts directly, stepping on an adjacent boundary rather than exposing a contract s1 can call

Blurs sc5's ownership: the HLD assigns the checkpoint record to s5 specifically so its internals (lc4: 'independent of ReviewContext's own fields') stay a separable, independently testable unit -- folding it into driver.ts makes the checkpoint logic untestable without also exercising the whole round cycle
Out of scope per the front-door rule: Story-scoped LLDs stay inside their own boundary and consume adjacent contracts, never re-implement or reach into them
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates sc1's HLD boundary by requiring edits to s1's privately-owned driver.ts internals, and blurs sc5's own separable, independently testable ownership (lc4).

alternativesConsidered.name: Generic reusable 'scratch side-record' abstraction
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A generalized, typed key-value side-record utility under .insrc/tmp/<id>/, with ReviewCheckpoint as its first consumer, anticipating future side-records other Stories might want.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Build a generic `SideRecord<T>` abstraction (read/write/finalize-and-cleanup parameterized over any JSON-serializable T and any id), then define ReviewCheckpoint as one instantiation of it, so any future Story needing a similar durable-scratch-record pattern reuses the same primitive.
pros: Would make a hypothetical future second side-record cheaper to add
cons: No other Story or contract in this Epic's HLD asks for a second side-record -- this generalizes for a need nobody has stated, directly against the instruction to add no option or flexibility nobody asked for
The extra type-parameterization and generic API surface make the one real consumer (ReviewCheckpoint) harder to read and test than a1's direct, concrete functions
Three concrete functions (a1) already fully satisfy every acceptance criterion; the generalization buys nothing measurable against this Story's own four ac's
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Technically satisfies every constraint but adds a generic SideRecord<T> abstraction no other Story or contract in this Epic's HLD asks for -- unrequested generalization at higher cost than a1 for no measurable benefit.
